papers.abstract_en: Immune heterogeneity and metabolic remodeling frequently limit the efficacy of immunotherapy in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). To address this challenge, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing analyses, pairing machine learning with preclinical models to develop the APOA5-correlated T-cell Signature (ACTsig), which effectively stratifies LUAD patients and predicts immunotherapeutic response. Moreover, We identified apolipoprotein A-V (APOA5) as a previously unrecognized tumor suppressor linking cholesterol homeostasis to the tumor immune ecosystem. Mechanistically, APOA5 deficiency induced intracellular cholesterol accumulation and MIF production. Cholesterol depletion and replenishment established a causal role for cholesterol accumulation in regulating MIF production, while MIF knockdown reversed APOA5-loss-induced T-cell exhaustion and recombinant MIF restored the phenotype. Meanwhile, CXCR4 blockade rescued APOA5-loss-induced T-cell exhaustion, supporting the functional involvement of the MIF receptor CXCR4 in this immunosuppressive phenotype. Finally, in silico drug screening identified fenofibrate, which, in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy, significantly suppressed tumor growth in APOA5-deficient models. Together, these findings establish ACTsig as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy response and reveal an APOA5-cholesterol-MIF-CXCR4 axis underlying T-cell exhaustion.

papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要未报告各标准对肺癌死亡率或筛查获益的验证，合格率仅为代理指标；研究人群为已确诊并接受手术的肺癌患者，不能反映筛查人群的假阳性、过度诊断或真实检出率，作者'改善公平与早期发现'的推论超出该设计可支持的范围；ORadj = 1.72（20年标准）所对应的人群归属（黑人或西班牙裔）在摘要中不明确，信息不足；未见参照组定义与多因素模型调整变量的说明。
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Although lung cancer screening reduces deaths, U.S. uptake is low, and disparities persist in eligibility. Our objectives were to evaluate how smoking intensity and duration shape screening eligibility across demographic groups and whether alternative criteria could promote more equitable screening. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of adults who underwent resection for primary lung cancer. Eligibility was defined using period-specific American Association for Thoracic Surgery (AATS) or U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) criteria and the following three alternative criteria: (1) one pack per day (PPD) (≥1 pack/d), (2) upper 75th (smoking duration ≥75% of lifetime), and (3) 20 years of smoking (YS) (≥20 y smoking). Multivariable linear models related demographics to smoking behaviors; logistic models estimated the odds of eligibility for each criterion. RESULTS: Smoking behaviors varied across demographic groups: female and racial and ethnic minority patients smoked at lower intensities but for longer durations comapred to White males. Among 995 participants, eligibility was 35.6% (AATS or USPSTF), 68.9% (one PPD), 25.9% (upper 75th), and 81.9% (20 YS), under the respective criteria. Females were less likely to be eligible under AATS or USPSTF (odds ratio [OR]adj = 0.65, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.50-0.85). Black patients had higher odds of eligibility under upper 75th (ORadj = 1.87, 95% CI: 1.27-2.72), as did Hispanic patients (ORadj = 1.99, 95% CI: 1.11-3.49), and under 20 YS (ORadj = 1.72, 95% CI: 1.07-2.89). Early stage (I or II, n = 910) cases captured as screening eligible varied by criteria: 35.7% (AATS or USPSTF), 68.6% (one PPD), 26.4% (upper 75th), and 81.9% (20 YS). CONCLUSION: Duration-focused eligibility criteria may better capture patient groups with low-intensity, long-duration smoking behaviors, potentially improving equity and early detection.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) addresses key limitations of traditional radiographic and tissue-based screening by providing a noninvasive alternative for the surveillance of NSCLC. In our study, we aim to evaluate trends in the performance of a commercially available methylation-based ctDNA test, characterize patient factors associated with fluctuating ctDNA positivity, and evaluate the clinical implications of serial monitoring. METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study included patients who underwent lung resection or stereotactic body radiation therapy for NSCLC followed by posttreatment ctDNA testing from 2024 to 2025. The primary outcomes include patient- and tumor-related risk factors associated with ctDNA positivity. A subgroup analysis of the ctDNA-positive group evaluated clinical events and genomic profiling that may influence transient ctDNA positivity. RESULTS: Of the 85 patients studied, 17 (20%) had at least one positive ctDNA test. Both ctDNA-positive and negative groups had similar patient and tumor-related features. Ten (59%) patients with a positive result subsequently tested negative, and 11 (65%) had a ctDNA tumor fraction near the limit of detection (LOD) without radiographic recurrence. No consistent associations were found with timing, adjuvant therapy, inflammatory markers, or tumor genomics. Three patients with ctDNA fractions above the limit of detection had confirmed recurrence; none in the ctDNA-negative group had disease recurrence. CONCLUSIONS: Although the utility of serial ctDNA testing is promising for NSCLC surveillance, isolated low-level positivity may not warrant clinical action. We observe frequent low-level, transient ctDNA positivity without radiographic evidence of recurrence, suggesting limitations in assay specificity and need for trend-based interpretation instead of isolated testing.

papers.authors: Wang D, Lin Y, Mei N, Du Y, Lu Y, Li X, Zhao Y, Ruan Z et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiology, Huashan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai, Shanghai, People's Republic of China.

papers.abstract_en: Methyltransferase-like 16 (METTL16), an m6A methyltransferase, regulates metal metabolism, but its role in copper homeostasis and cuproptosis in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unknown. Using ESCC cells exposed to CuCl2 or cuproptosis inducers, RNA interference, multi-omics, reader screening, and protein-turnover assays, we dissected the ZDHHC20-METTL16-STEAP1 axis. Xenograft and 4NQO-induced models, TCGA/GTEx datasets, and tissue microarrays were used for in vivo and prognostic analyses. Copper stress upregulated METTL16 and m6A modifications. METTL16 silencing reduced sensitivity to elesclomol-Cu/disulfiram-induced cuproptosis, which was rescued by STEAP1 overexpression. Mechanistically, METTL16 stabilized STEAP1 mRNA via m6A modification at position 286 with YTHDC1, enhancing cuproptosis sensitivity. Conversely, ZDHHC20 mediated METTL16 palmitoylation and cytoplasmic retention, suppressing STEAP1 stabilization and increasing cuproptosis resistance; ZDHHC20 depletion altered METTL16 localization without affecting its abundance or turnover. In vivo, ZDHHC20 knockout reduced esophageal lesion burden, whereas METTL16-IN-1 or vandortuzumab vedotin administration was associated with increased lesion burden in knockout mice. The VDM-associated observations did not establish STEAP1-specific inhibition in vivo. High ZDHHC20 correlated with poor prognosis, while elevated METTL16/STEAP1 predicted better survival. Targeting the ZDHHC20-METTL16-STEAP1 axis may overcome cuproptosis resistance in ESCC.

papers.authors: Gallina FT, Ambrosi F, Marinelli D, Guerrera F, Sepulcri M, Viscardi G, Bertoglio P, Di Federico A et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Thoracic-Surgery Unit, Istituto di Ricovero e Cura a Carattere Scientifico Regina Elena National Cancer Institute, Rome,…

papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要未报告达成共识的量化阈值（如同意比例、9点量表得分界值）、各条声明的具体评分分布、专家人数与应答率，也未说明是否进行证据等级评定或文献支持，故无法评估共识强度与偏倚风险；共识不等于疗效证据，条目结论（如可切除III期优选新辅助免疫化疗、全肺切除限于高度选择病例）系专家意见而非试验数据，不应作为疗效依据引用
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Stage III NSCLC represents one of the most heterogeneous and clinically challenging scenarios in thoracic oncology. The rapid integration of immunotherapy into multimodal treatment strategies has reshaped therapeutic algorithms, particularly for resectable and borderline resectable diseases. However, uncertainty persists regarding optimal staging procedures, resectability assessment, and the integration of surgery, systemic therapy, and radiotherapy. METHODS: A multisocietal Delphi consensus was conducted to address key areas of uncertainty in the multidisciplinary management of stage III NSCLC. Experts in thoracic surgery, medical oncology, radiation oncology, interventional pulmonology, and pathology, nominated by four Italian scientific societies, participated in a structured consensus process. Sixty-five statements covering baseline evaluation, local treatment, and integrated therapeutic strategies were rated using a 9-point Likert scale across two Delphi rounds. RESULTS: Consensus was achieved for 62 of 65 statements. Strong agreement supported comprehensive baseline staging, including contrast-enhanced computed tomography, positron emission tomography imaging, brain magnetic resonance imaging, and systematic mediastinal staging with endosonographic techniques. Molecular characterization, including Programmed Death-Ligand 1 expression and testing for EGFR and ALK alterations, was considered essential for treatment selection. Neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy was endorsed as the preferred strategy for most patients with resectable stage III NSCLC without actionable driver alterations. Lung-sparing surgical procedures were strongly favored, while pneumonectomy should be reserved for highly selected cases. For unresectable disease, concurrent chemoradiotherapy followed by consolidation immunotherapy remains the standard of care. CONCLUSION: This multidisciplinary consensus provides an updated framework for the contemporary management of stage III NSCLC, emphasizing accurate staging, molecular profiling, and coordinated multidisciplinary decision-making to optimize multimodal treatment strategies.

papers.authors: He Y, Dong X, Yun L, Song K, Zhou Z, Jiang J, Ge H, Zhang R et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: These findings identify condensate-mediated spatial control of pyroptosis as a mechanism of chemoprotection and suggest MAGEA6 phase separation as a potential therapeutic target in cisplatin-resistant ESCC.
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要全部为定性表述，无任何效应量、样本量、统计检验与P/CI；模型种类（细胞系/类器官/动物）与体内抑瘤或顺铂增敏数据未报告；MAGEA6作为治疗靶点的可成药性与正常组织（睾丸等）毒性未评估；ESCC中MAGEA6表达与患者顺铂疗效/预后的临床关联未提供。
papers.abstract_en: Chemotherapy can trigger pyroptosis in cancer cells, yet the intrinsic regulatory mechanisms governing this process remain largely unclear. Here, we identify MAGEA6 as a phase-separating cancer-testis antigen that establishes a pyroptosis-suppressive condensate barrier in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) by coordinately restraining GSDMD and GSDME cleavage. Mechanistically, cytoplasm-anchored MAGEA6 undergoes phase separation, which impedes the nuclear translocation of TP63, thereby suppressing NLRP1 transcription and subsequent GSDMD activation. Concurrently, MAGEA6 recruits GSDME into dynamic condensates and restricts its Caspase-3-mediated cleavage in response to cisplatin. Disruption of MAGEA6 condensation relieved both inhibitory effects, whereas the MAGEA6 intrinsically disordered region was sufficient to sustain the chemoprotective condensate state. Perturbation of this condensate barrier restored pyroptotic signaling and increased cisplatin sensitivity across multiple ESCC models. These findings identify condensate-mediated spatial control of pyroptosis as a mechanism of chemoprotection and suggest MAGEA6 phase separation as a potential therapeutic target in cisplatin-resistant ESCC.

papers.title_en: A mouse neuroimmune circuit that regulates allergic inflammation in the esophagus.
papers.authors: Kellerman KM, Rochman M, Natale MA, Gerstner E, Rochman Y, Golosarsky T, Caldwell JM, Felton JM et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Allergy and Immunology, Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center, Cincinnati, OH, USA.
papers.authors_conclusion: Our findings thus describe a type 2 neuroimmune circuit that potentially contributes to EoE pathogenesis, including pain.
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要为纯机制叙述，未报告任何样本量、效应量、CI或P值，无法评估效应大小与统计学稳健性；动物实验的随机化、盲法、性别与品系等关键方法学信息缺失；患者样本验证仅定性描述'neuronal density increased'，无定量数据与病例特征；结论为'potentially contributes'，属探索性关联而非因果证实，临床转化（如Nav1.8/IGF-1靶向镇痛）证据尚远。
papers.abstract_en: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic, allergic disease associated with refractory pain in patients, yet the function of the nervous system in EoE pathogenesis remains ill-defined. Here we elucidate a mouse neuroimmune circuit that is linked to type 2-associated allergic inflammation and clinical responses in the esophagus, including pain. In a mouse allergy model, allergen exposure evokes pain-like behavior, increases esophageal Nav1.8+ sensory innervation density, and alters nociceptor sensitization. Thoracic dorsal root ganglia (DRG) show expression of type 2 cytokine receptors Il4ra and Il13ra1, and IL-4 and IL-13 sensitize DRG neurons to noxious agents. Mechanistically, conditional deletion of Il4ra in mouse NaV1.8+ neurons attenuate the above allergen-induced phenotypes as well as the levels of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1); in parallel, IGF-1 receptor inhibition also dampens these disease features. Finally, EoE patient samples show increased esophageal neuronal density when compared with controls. Our findings thus describe a type 2 neuroimmune circuit that potentially contributes to EoE pathogenesis, including pain.

papers.title_en: A Comparison of the Global and Berlin Definitions of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
papers.authors: Smoker L, Dongre Y, Bhakta S, Kimbrell JM, Butler T, Gope A, Chandra F, Yuan C et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Critical Care Medicine, Department of Medicine, Montefiore Medical Center, Bronx, NY, USA.
papers.authors_conclusion: 与Berlin定义相比，Global ARDS定义纳入了更多急性低氧衰竭患者为ARDS；起初仅符合Global标准者中只有一小部分进展为符合Berlin定义；仅符合Global定义而未进展为Berlin定义的患者死亡率高，但该死亡很大一部分发生在与气管插管相关的限制治疗指令背景下。
papers.ai_note: 37.8% vs 26.7%的病死率差异为观察性关联：进展至Berlin标准需存活至更重低氧血症阶段，存在病情严重度与时间相关偏倚，不能解读为定义本身的预后判别力；摘要未报告两定义的AUROC/校准或一致性检验(kappa)，预后验证信息不足。Global-only组被作者概括为高死亡率，但其中76.2%死亡发生于DNI/DNR限制治疗背景下，属选择性强调风险。单一医疗系统回顾性数据，影像由两名研究者独立复核但未说明是否对结局设盲，外部验证缺失。
papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: The Global definition of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) expands Berlin criteria to include SpO2:FiO2 ratios, High-Flow Nasal Cannula (HFNC), lung ultrasound, and non-intubated patients outside the critical care setting. We aimed to characterize the prevalence, progression, and outcomes of ARDS as defined by the Global and Berlin definitions. METHODS: We included adult patients admitted to multiple hospitals within a single health system between December 1, 2021 and May 31, 2022 who met criteria for ARDS according to either the Global or Berlin definition within the first 7 days of hospitalization. Chest imaging was reviewed independently by two investigators for new bilateral opacities not attributable to atelectasis, effusion, mass, or heart failure. RESULTS: Among 3,342 admissions screened for Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure (AHRF), 1,220 (36.5%) met Global ARDS criteria, of whom 535 (43.9%) met Berlin criteria at some point during hospitalization. Of these 535, 381 (71.2%) met both definitions simultaneously, and 154 (28.8%) initially met only Global criteria before subsequently meeting Berlin criteria, a median of 1 day later (IQR 1-3). The remaining 685 (56.1%) met Global criteria only and never progressed to Berlin ARDS. Patients meeting Berlin criteria at any time had higher mortality than those who never met Berlin criteria (37.8% vs. 26.7%, p < 0.001). Among the 246 HFNC-managed patients who never progressed to Berlin criteria, 84 (34.1%) died, with care-limitation directives (do-not-intubate [DNI] and/or do-not-resuscitate [DNR]) present in 103 (41.9%) and accounting for 64 (76.2%) of deaths in this group. CONCLUSIONS: As compared to the Berlin definition of ARDS, the Global ARDS definition captures more patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure as having ARDS. Of those initially meeting only Global criteria, only a fraction progress to meet the Berlin definition. Patients meeting only the Global definition of ARDS without progression to the Berlin definition have a high mortality rate; however, much of this mortality occurs in the context of care-limitation directives related to tracheal intubation.

papers.abstract_en: Interleukin-33 (IL-33) from lung epithelial cells serves as a crucial alarmin to activate the lung-resident group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) and then to initiate type 2 inflammation. However, whether IL-33 has an intrinsic role in the ILC2-driven lung inflammation remains unclear. In this study, we characterize the proteomic features of mouse lung ILC2s during activation and observe an increased expression of intrinsic IL-33 in activated ILC2s. The expression of intrinsic IL-33 in lung ILC2s can be induced by the co-stimulation of cysteinyl leukotrienes (CysLTs) and exogenous IL-33. Deletion of ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 attenuates lung inflammation by restraining ILC2 proliferation and cytokine production. Mechanistically, ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 promotes transcriptional activation of both inflammatory and proliferative signaling cascades. Additionally, ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 localizes in the nucleus and promotes the expression of Fosl2 and Nfatc1 through promoting their chromatin accessibility, leading to increased ILC2 proliferation and type 2 cytokine production. Further, we confirm that intrinsic IL-33 can be induced by co-stimulation of CysLTs and exogenous IL-33 in human ILC2s (hILC2s), which is positively related to enhanced hILC2 responses. Collectively, our findings implicate IL-33 as a nuclear factor and intrinsic amplifier of lung-resident ILC2s, operating in a positive feedback loop downstream of exogenous IL-33 and CysLTs co-stimulation to promote allergic lung inflammation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is a labeled risk of elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) that most often arises within the first year of therapy; elevations beyond that window are incompletely characterized. We hypothesized that new liver test elevations occur after the first year and are associated with identifiable host- and exposure-related risk factors. METHODS: Single-center retrospective cohort study of 124 adults with cystic fibrosis (CF) who received ETI for at least 12 months. Delayed liver test (dLT) elevations were defined as elevations occurring more than 12 months after initiation. RESULTS: Thirty-six patients (29%) developed new alanine aminotransferase (ALT) elevations beyond 12 months, of whom 6 (16.7%) had no identifiable alternative contributor and were attributed to ETI. Delayed elevations were associated with male sex (p = 0.04), F508del homozygosity (p = 0.05), prior CF liver disease (p < 0.001), acetaminophen exposure (p = 0.007), and concurrent infection or inflammation (p = 0.002). Six patients had clinically significant elevations exceeding 3 times the upper limit of normal (ULN); in these, total bilirubin remained normal and hepatic imaging and elastography identified no alternative etiology, and Roussel Uclaf Causality Assessment Method scoring classified five as "possible" and one as "probable" DILI. ETI dose reduction normalized or stabilized ALT in most, with only modest spirometric change. CONCLUSIONS: New liver test elevations occurred after the first year of ETI in a substantial minority of adults with CF, and in 16.7% no alternative cause was identified. These findings support continued, risk-informed liver test monitoring beyond the first year.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical, radiological and treatment characteristics of patients diagnosed with nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) between 2012 and 2017. In addition, we investigated the association of these findings with survival outcomes in the context of contemporary treatment strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective cohort study included 79 patients with NSIP. Demographic data, comorbidities, modified Medical Research Council dyspnoea scores, high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) findings, pulmonary function test results, administered immunosuppressive agents and clinical course data were recorded. RESULTS: The mean age of the cohort was 66.3 ± 10.3 (range: 41-87) years, and 45.6% and 54.4% of them were female and male, respectively. At least one comorbidity was present in 78.5% of patients, cardiovascular disease being the most frequent. Ground-glass opacity was the most common thoracic HRCT finding (91.1%). A honeycombing pattern was present in 40.5% of patients and was associated with mortality (log-rank p = 0.009; univariable Cox HR 3.49, 95% CI 1.29-9.46). Immunosuppressive therapy was administered to 74.6% of patients. There was no significant difference in the survival of the treated and untreated groups (log-rank p = 0.320). Overall survival was calculated as 66.1 months (95% CI: 58.7-73.5). CONCLUSION: The results suggest that a honeycombing pattern may be associated with a worse prognosis in NSIP. The width of the confidence interval and the modest number of events mean this should be regarded as a hypothesis-generating observation requiring prospective confirmation. No significant survival difference was observed between treated and untreated patients, although the small number of events in the untreated group limits the interpretation of this comparison. These findings support the individualisation of treatment decisions in NSIP based on clinical and radiological prognostic features.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is associated with substantial symptom burden and limited survival. Recent advances in pleural interventions, molecular diagnostics and prognostic tools are challenging traditional approaches to management. This review summarizes recent developments and considers how these may support more personalised care. RECENT FINDINGS: Indwelling pleural catheters (IPCs) and talc pleurodesis remain the principal definitive treatment strategies, with increasing evidence supporting individualized selection according to lung expandability, prognosis, treatment burden and patient preference. Accelerated diagnostic and therapeutic pathways may reduce repeated procedures. The RED score may help estimate time to further pleural intervention, pending broader validation and evaluation of clinical utility. Patient-reported outcomes and treatment burden are increasingly recognized as important measures of treatment success. SUMMARY: MPE management should integrate tumour biology, pleural physiology, prognosis and patient preferences. Emerging diagnostic, prognostic and technological advances may further enable personalized, patient-centred care.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Accumulating evidence suggests a significant link between dyslipidaemia-characterized by an imbalance in circulating lipids and lipoproteins-and the pathogenesis and progression of various chronic respiratory conditions. However, their mechanistic role in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) pathogenesis has yet to be fully elucidated. This study aimed to explore the associations of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) with TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C in Chinese adults. METHODS: This study included 129 patients in the stable phase of IPF, 85 patients with acute exacerbation (AE-IPF), and 130 non-IPF controls. The evaluation included routine blood tests (encompassing the lipid profile) and pulmonary function assessments. Additionally, a follow-up with a median duration of 5.84 months was conducted in 183 IPF patients. RESULTS: Compared with values observed in stable cases or control subjects, the levels of both TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C were markedly elevated in subjects with AE-IPF. Following adjustment for potential confounders, logistic regression models revealed that both TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C were independent factors positively correlated with the presence of AE-IPF. In assessing the predictive power for AE-IPF, the area under the ROC curve corresponding to TG/HDL-C exceeded that of TC/HDL-C and all other conventional lipid levels. During a median follow-up of 5.84 months, 81 IPF patients passed away. Nonsurvivors had higher baseline TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C levels than survivors did. Multivariate Cox regression analysis adjusted for age, sex, and oxygenation index revealed that the adjusted hazard ratios for overall survival with each 1-SD increase in TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C were 1.809 (95% CI: 1.497-2.184, P < 0.001) and 1.486 (95% CI: 1.183-1.867, P = 0.001), respectively. CONCLUSION: Elevated TG/HDL-C and TC/HDL-C ratios are independently associated with acute exacerbation and poor short-term survival in IPF patients. The TG/HDL-C ratio, in particular, represents a candidate biomarker for risk stratification, which requires further external validation.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Bronchoscopic lung volume reduction (BLVR) with endobronchial valves is effective primarily in patients without collateral ventilation (CV-), leaving limited options for patients with collateral ventilation (CV+) in the target lobe. AeriSeal, delivered bronchoscopically, may occlude collateral channels and enable subsequent valve treatment. OBJECTIVES: To prospectively evaluate whether AeriSeal can convert target lobes from CV+ to CV- status in severe emphysema, enabling subsequent treatment with Zephyr valves. METHODS: Patients with severe COPD/emphysema, fissure completeness ≥80% on quantitative CT, and Chartis-confirmed collateral ventilation-positive (CV+) status were enrolled. Eligible subjects had fissure defects involving no more than three segmental airways. AeriSeal foam (≤40 mL) was administered bronchoscopically in one or two sessions, and CV status was reassessed after 6 weeks. Subjects converting to CV- status underwent Zephyr valve placement. Primary endpoints were successful CV conversion and target lobe volume reduction (TLVR ≥350 mL) 45 days after valve implantation. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 101 subjects, 75/99 evaluable patients achieved CV conversion (75.8%; 95% exact CI, 66.1-83.8%). Following valve treatment, TLVR ≥350 mL was achieved in 64/72 evaluable subjects (88.9%; 95% exact CI, 79.3-95.1%), with mean TLVR of 1062.5 ± 676.2 mL at 45 days, sustained through 12 months. At 6 months, post-bronchodilator FEV₁ improved by 0.08 L, residual volume decreased by 0.49L, SGRQ improved by 6.4 points, and mMRC by 0.8 points. Common serious adverse events included post-acute inflammatory response (PAIR; 16.7%), pneumothorax (19.2% within 45 days post-valves), COPD exacerbation, and pneumonia. Three deaths occurred, including one probably valve-related. CONCLUSIONS: AeriSeal effectively converts collateral ventilation status in most treated patients, enabling successful valve therapy with durable lobar volume reduction and acceptable safety.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive, fatal interstitial lung disease with limited therapies that only delay progression. Stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) offer a promising cell-free alternative due to their immunomodulatory, anti-fibrotic, and regenerative properties. AREAS COVERED: This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms by which EVs secreted from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells, adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells, bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, and induced pluripotent stem cells inhibit pulmonary fibrosis. The article compares various administration routes and highlights nebulized inhalation as an effective delivery strategy. It also provides a rigorous evaluation of the complete clinical-grade manufacturing workflow, including stem cell culture, extracellular vesicle isolation and purification, quality control, and preservation. We have referenced relevant English medical literature from the Medline/PubMed database up to September 2026. EXPERT OPINION: Major barriers to clinical translation include donor heterogeneity, lack of standardized Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) protocols, and storage instability. Future advances will rely on engineered EV modifications, Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC)-based scalable production. Within five years, nebulized MSC-EV products are expected to enter clinical practice, shifting IPF treatment from fibrosis delay toward repair, alongside existing oral anti-fibrotics.

papers.abstract_en: Sarcoidosis-associated pulmonary hypertension (SAPH) is a significant yet often overlooked complication of sarcoidosis that profoundly affects both morbidity and mortality rates. The development of SAPH illustrates the intricate relationship among lung tissue damage, granulomatous inflammation of blood vessels, and remodeling of cardiac or vascular structures. This complexity highlights the multifaceted nature of sarcoidosis pathophysiology. In this review, we delve into key topics, including epidemiology, underlying mechanisms, and current treatment options, while also discussing the path forward for precision medicine applications. SAPH serves as a clear example of the systemic and vascular intricacies of sarcoidosis, connecting immune-mediated granulomatous inflammation with pulmonary vascular involvement. By gaining a deeper understanding of its unique molecular, hemodynamic, and imaging characteristics, we can enhance risk stratification and therapeutic decision-making, ultimately paving the way for more tailored management of sarcoidosis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Elarekibep (AZD1402/PRS-060) is an Anticalin, a new class of inhaled therapeutic proteins, which has been engineered to inhibit interleukin-4 receptor α-subunit (IL-4Rα) signalling, a key target in asthma. METHODS: Two phase 1 randomized, first-in-human, dose-escalating, single-blind studies (NCT03384290; NCT03574805) investigated single ascending doses (SADs) or multiple ascending doses (MADs) of elarekibep compared with placebo. In the SAD study, healthy participants received a single inhaled dose of elarekibep 0.1-160 mg, intravenous doses of 1 mg or 2 mg, or matched placebo. In the MAD study, participants with mild asthma and elevated fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) received inhaled doses of elarekibep 0.2-60 mg or placebo twice daily for 10 or 17 days (single dose on day 10 in all but one cohort), continuously or intermittently. RESULTS: In total, 148 participants were enrolled across both studies. No safety concerns were reported. Treatment-emergent adverse events were experienced by 34.7% (elarekibep, 35.2%; placebo, 33.3%) and 81.6% (elarekibep, 75.9%; placebo, 95.5%) of SAD and MAD study participants, respectively. Elarekibep was absorbed after inhalation, with dose-related increases in systemic exposure detectable with doses greater than or equal to 6 mg. In both studies, systemic exposure resulted in decreased levels of phosphorylated signal transducer and activator of transcription 6, a biomarker for systemic IL-4Rα target engagement. In the MAD study, rapid reductions of FeNO were demonstrated with doses greater than or equal to 2 mg, indicating pulmonary target engagement. CONCLUSIONS: Elarekibep was well tolerated in both studies and demonstrated pulmonary and systemic target engagement. Elarekibep was investigated further in a phase 2a study (NCT04643158). TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT03384290. Registered 26 November 2017, https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03384290 . NCT03574805. Registered 2 July 2018, https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03574805 .

papers.abstract_en: RATIONAL: In Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), as disease severity worsens, lung function declines and symptom burden increases. The characteristics of individuals with severe airflow limitation who report no dyspnea (eupnea) are not well described. OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether eupneic individuals with severe airflow limitation exhibit different clinical and imaging characteristics compared to those who are dyspneic. METHODS: We analyzed data from 1,713 COPDGene participants with GOLD 3-4, categorized by mMRC dyspnea scores: 0 (eupneic), 1-2, and 3-4. Baseline assessments included spirometry, CT imaging, six-minute walk, and symptom questionnaires. Longitudinal outcomes included FEV1 decline, exacerbation frequency, and mortality. We replicated the analysis in participants with GOLD 1-2, GOLD 0, and preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm). RESULTS: Among GOLD 3-4 participants, 8.2% were eupneic. Compared to those with mMRC 3-4, eupneic individuals had lower prevalence of chronic bronchitis and worse health-related quality of life, better exercise capacity, and less CT emphysema, gas trapping, and PRMfSAD. They experienced fewer exacerbations [incidence rate ratio (IRR) = 0.54; 95% CI: 0.42-0.69; P < 0.001] and had lower mortality (HR = 0.62;95% CI 0.48-0.80). Rates of longitudinal FEV1 decline were similar across mMRC groups. We observed similar findings in the GOLD 1-2, GOLD 0, and PRISm analyses. CONCLUSIONS: A modest proportion of individuals with severe respiratory function impairment are eupneic, showing better clinical outcomes and less structural lung damage than their dyspneic counterparts. Our findings support a multidimensional COPD assessment that incorporates symptom burden alongside spirometry.

papers.abstract_en: AbstractAI models using medical images are increasingly proposed to support clinical decision-making in lung cancer, motivating assessment of their methodological rigor and transparency. To assess how these models are developed, evaluated, and reported, and to identify gaps in best statistical practices, we conducted a cross-sectional meta-research review of OpenAlex-indexed studies (January 1, 2023, to June 30, 2025) that developed image-based AI tools for lung cancer risk prediction, detection, or prognosis. Thirty-six studies met our inclusion criteria. Convolutional neural networks were used in most studies (27 studies, 75%), and area under the curve (AUC) was the most frequently reported evaluation metric (29 studies, 81%). Although 23 studies (64%) reported some form of uncertainty quantification, most were limited to presenting confidence intervals for global performance metrics (e.g., AUC, sensitivity, and accuracy) rather than individual prediction- or risk-level uncertainty. Common limitations included limited external test set use (14 studies, 39%), insufficient subgroup analyses (10 studies, 28%), and limited adherence to established prediction-model reporting guidelines. Overall, future research should prioritize standardized reporting, use of external test sets, and model performance assessment across clinically relevant subpopulations. The coexistence of increasingly powerful AI-based prediction models with inconsistent study design, evaluation, and reporting practices emphasizes the urgent need to implement more rigorous and transparent methodological standards in this field. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Stroke affects approximately 140,000 patients annually in France and is the second leading cause of mortality after cancer. Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), particularly obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), worsens functional recovery and increases mortality risk after stroke. The objective of this study was to evaluate markers of nocturnal hypoxaemia recorded during cardiorespiratory Holter monitoring in patients hospitalised for a first ischaemic stroke and to assess their association with all-cause mortality. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, observational, single-centre longitudinal study including adult patients hospitalised for ischaemic stroke at Saint-Etienne University Hospital (January 2010-December 2020) who underwent cardiorespiratory Holter monitoring. Five nocturnal hypoxaemia markers were analysed: mean nocturnal SpO2, oxygen desaturation index (ODI), time spent with SpO2 below 90% (T90), mean desaturation duration, and mean slope of desaturation. All-cause mortality was ascertained from the French national INSEE death registry (census date: 23 December 2023). Cox proportional hazards models and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed. RESULTS: Of 3595 patients hospitalised for stroke, 1113 met inclusion criteria (mean age 65.8 ± 14.4 years; 61% male). At census, 288 deaths had been recorded (mean time to death: 1532 days). Mean nocturnal SpO2 below 90% was associated with mortality (HR 1.46; 95% CI 1.04-2.04; p = 0.028). ODI ≥15/h was associated with mortality (HR 1.58; 95% CI 1.24-2.00; p = 0.00016). T90 ≥ 10% was associated with mortality (HR 1.34; 95% CI 1.05-1.72; p = 0.02). Desaturation duration and slope were not significantly associated with mortality. CONCLUSION: Mean nocturnal SpO2 below 90%, ODI ≥15/h, and T90 ≥ 10% are associated with all-cause mortality in post-ischaemic stroke patients. These markers are readily obtainable by nocturnal oximetry in neurovascular units and may facilitate early identification of high-risk patients.

papers.abstract_en: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) pneumonia represents a critical threat owing to its high mortality and antibiotic resistance. Near-infrared II (NIR-II) fluorescent photothermal therapy (PTT) enables deep-tissue heating but risks incomplete bacterial clearance and thermal damage. Symmetric donor-acceptor-donor (D-A-D) NIR-II molecules often suffer from high molecular weights, low fluorescence, and suboptimal photothermal conversion. Herein, we report asymmetric D-A-π-D NIR-II aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) featuring a benzothiopyrylium acceptor, triphenylamine donors, and furan or thiophene as π-bridge. Furan strengthens non-covalent conformation locking while weakening intermolecular π-π stacking, thereby enhancing both fluorescence and photothermal performance. AIEgen 4fop achieves an optimal photothermal conversion efficiency of 84.3% and a NIR-II photoluminescence quantum yield of 2.31% in toluene. To boost antibacterial activity, 4fop was co-encapsulated with the thermally responsive NO donor BNN6 into Pluronic F-127 nanoparticles. In a murine pneumonia model, this nanoplatform substantially reduces bacterial burden, suppresses inflammation through TNF pathway modulation, and promotes lung repair. This work establishes a rational D-A-π-D design strategy and an integrated nanoplatform for the precise treatment of deep-seated drug-resistant infections.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: While several G2/M oncogenes are known to promote tumor progression, their coordinated tumor-suppressive networks antagonizing this axis and their regulatory and immunological contexts remain poorly defined. METHODS: We performed a multi-layered integrative analysis combining correlation profiling (UALCAN and ENCORI), multi-endpoint survival analysis (KM Plotter: OS, FPS, PPS across pan-lung, LUAD, and smoker cohorts), and transcriptomic refinement using TNMplot. A miRNA-mRNA regulatory network was constructed via miRNet, refined using UALCAN expression filtering, KM survival, and CancerMIRNome ROC analysis, followed by ENCORI-based miRNA-gene correlation. Direct miRNA-mRNA and lncRNA-miRNA binding affinities were assessed using IntaRNA. lncRNAs associated with the key miRNA were identified via Enrichr, filtered by expression, correlation, and survival, and validated by binding and gene correlation analyses. Finally, immune cell correlations were evaluated using GSCA, and an integrated ROC model was generated in R. RESULTS: We identified a high-confidence panel of six tumor suppressors (CBX7, CD81, CRY2, CYBRD1, NR3C2, REEP5) and six G2/M oncogenes (AURKA, AURKB, BUB1, FOXM1, MELK, TTK) based on correlation, survival, and TNMplot criteria. hsa-let-7b-5p emerged as a central regulatory miRNA (AUC = 0.89) positively correlated with tumor suppressors and predicted to bind all six oncogenes. TMPO-AS1 was identified as an oncogenic lncRNA antagonizing hsa-let-7b-5p via strong binding (-15.85 kcal/mol) and negative correlation with tumor suppressors. An integrated lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA ROC model achieved an AUC ≈ 0.97. Immune analysis revealed reciprocal patterns: tumor suppressors correlated with MAIT, NKT, and Tfh cells and inversely with exhausted cells and nTregs, whereas oncogenes showed the opposite trend with the same. CONCLUSION: This study defines a robust G2/M -associated regulatory framework in LUAD, characterized by reciprocal dysregulation of oncogenes and tumor suppressors and associated with the predicted TMPO-AS1-hsa-let-7b-5p regulatory network, which is linked to a less immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, offering potential prognostic and therapeutic implications in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: Influenza viruses continually evolve through antigenic drift and shift, spreading via respiratory droplets and aerosols. Developing a universal nasal vaccine is essential for preventing seasonal and pandemic infections by inducing long-lasting immunity in the respiratory tract. The neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) transfers IgG Abs across the epithelial barrier. This study investigates whether the i.n. delivery of the conserved Stalk antigen of HA, utilizing the FcRn, can stimulate protective immune responses against various influenza virus subtypes. We engineered a monomeric IgG Fc fused to a modified HA Stalk in its prefusion form. Mice i.n. immunized with Stalk-Fc exhibited significant protection against infections from H1N1, H5N1, H6N2, and H9N2 compared with groups of control mice. The immunized mice produced long-lasting HA Stalk-specific IgA and IgG Abs in nasal washes, bronchoalveolar lavage, and blood, along with tissue-resident memory T cells in the lungs and long-lived plasma cells in the bone marrow. This led to notably lower viral replication in the nasal turbinate and lungs. The Stalk-specific Abs demonstrated strong cross-reactivity against different influenza subtypes through neutralization, Ab- or complement-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, or phagocytosis. These results indicate that FcRn efficiently transports HA Stalk-Fc across the respiratory epithelial barrier, supporting the development of a universal influenza nasal vaccine.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) remains a major public health challenge in Nigeria, with gaps in treatment enrolment and completion undermining control efforts. This study assessed MDR-TB treatment outcomes and explored caregivers' perspectives on factors influencing treatment enrolment and adherence in Oyo State, Nigeria. METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional mixed-methods study was conducted in Oyo State, Nigeria. The quantitative component involved retrospective review of 277 MDR-TB patient records from accredited treatment facilities between 2016 and 2022, while the qualitative component comprised in-depth interviews with 10 purposively selected caregivers, including healthcare workers, tuberculosis and leprosy supervisors, and community-based organization representatives involved in MDR-TB care. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests at p < 0.05, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically. Analysis of MDR-TB case detection and enrolment was restricted to 2020-2022 due to availability of complete surveillance records. RESULTS: Most patients were aged ≥ 30 years (70.4%) and male (52.3%). Between 2020 and 2022, a total of 716 MDR-TB cases were detected, of which 295 (42.2%) were enrolled in treatment, with enrolment improving to 51.3% in 2022. Among the enrolled patients, 75.8% achieved successful treatment outcomes, including 63.2% who completed treatment and 12.6% who were cured, while 24.2% experienced unfavorable outcomes such as loss to follow-up (11.6%) and death (6.9%). No statistically significant associations were observed between socio-demographic or clinical characteristics and treatment outcomes (p > 0.05). Qualitative findings identified perceived treatment effectiveness, counselling, free treatment services, financial and social support, and strong health system follow-up as major facilitators of treatment enrolment and adherence. Key barriers included poverty, stigma, prolonged treatment duration, poor adherence, and disruption of livelihoods. CONCLUSION: Although MDR-TB treatment outcomes were relatively successful in Oyo State, significant gaps remain in treatment enrolment and completion. Strengthening patient support systems, addressing socioeconomic barriers, and improving linkage between diagnosis and treatment initiation are essential to improving MDR-TB control. Caregiver perspectives provide important insights for strengthening program implementation and patient retention. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. This study was a descriptive cross-sectional mixed-methods study involving retrospective record review and qualitative interviews, and therefore did not require clinical trial registration.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) have reduced pulmonary reserve and increased susceptibility to airborne pollutants. However, practical guidance for managing residential indoor air quality (IAQ) remains limited. Objectives: To review evidence and reference standards relevant to IAQ management in COPD and IPF and propose practical, disease-informed recommendations for reducing indoor pollutant exposure. METHODS: We conducted a focused narrative review of evidence on pollutant exposure, respiratory health effects, and residential exposure-reduction interventions. Domestic and international indoor and ambient air quality standards were reviewed to identify key management parameters and feasible exposure-reduction strategies. Separate decision rules were applied to action references and maintenance targets according to exposure setting, intended use, and source-specific averaging time. RESULTS: Nine parameters were selected: PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO2, formaldehyde, total volatile organic compounds, CO, O3, and relative humidity. Where applicable, action references indicated conditions under which exposure-reduction measures should be considered, whereas maintenance targets supported routine exposure management. Ambient forecast categories were used only for pollutants primarily managed according to outdoor conditions. CO2 and relative humidity were treated as operational environmental parameters. All values retained the averaging times and intended contexts of their source standards and were not considered disease-specific clinical cutoffs. Recommendations emphasized source control, outdoor air quality-guided ventilation, particle filtration, and control of cooking and combustion emissions. CONCLUSION: This framework provides practical, parameter-specific exposure-management references and strategies for patients with COPD and IPF. Prospective studies should assess whether multicomponent IAQ interventions improve exposure and clinically relevant respiratory outcomes.
